valid.name: dot access - never a computed member expression

valid.name: string-literal key - V8 folds it to the same GetNamedProperty bytecode as dot access
valid.code: declare const record: Record<string, unknown>; const value = record['alpha'];

valid.name: numeric-literal key - statically known, not a dynamic lookup
valid.code: declare const record: Record<number, unknown>; const value = record[42];

valid.name: array index by variable - elements store, never transitions the hidden class
valid.code: declare const values: readonly number[]; declare const index: number; const value = values[index];

valid.name: array index assignment by variable - same elements-store reasoning
valid.code: declare const values: number[]; declare const index: number; values[index] = 1;

valid.name: typed-array index by variable - FLOAT64ELEMENTS store, map unchanged

valid.name: tuple index by variable - isTupleType exemption
valid.code: declare const pair: readonly [number, string]; declare const index: number; const value = pair[index];

valid.name: string index by variable - character access, not a named property
valid.code: declare const text: string; declare const index: number; const value = text[index];

valid.name: array possibly undefined - union-aware exemption
valid.code: declare const values: readonly number[] | undefined; declare const index: number; const value = values === undefined ? 0 : values[index];

valid.name: well-known symbol key - Symbol.iterator has no non-computed spelling in JavaScript
valid.code: declare const values: readonly number[]; const iterator = values[Symbol.iterator]();

valid.name: index loop over an array - the fast path for-of-arrays mandates, 3.9ms vs 26.9ms at 5M
valid.code: declare const values: readonly number[]; let total = 0; const length = values.length; for (let index = 0; index < length; index += 1) { total += values[index] ?? 0; }

valid.name: variable key read on a plain object - a read cannot enter dictionary mode
valid.code: declare const record: Record<string, unknown>; declare const key: string; const value = record[key];

valid.name: read: variable key on a plain object inside a loop
valid.code: declare const record: Record<string, unknown>; declare const keys: readonly string[]; const length = keys.length; for (let index = 0; index < length; index += 1) { const key = keys[index] ?? ''; const value = record[key]; }

valid.name: read: variable key on an interface-typed object
valid.code: interface ShapeInterface { readonly alpha: number; readonly beta: number; } declare const shape: ShapeInterface; declare const key: 'alpha' | 'beta'; const value = shape[key];

valid.name: read: computed access on a plain object nested inside an object literal
valid.code: declare const record: Record<string, unknown>; declare const key: string; const wrapper = { 'value': record[key] };

valid.name: Reflect.set with a literal key - same GetNamedProperty fold as bracket-literal write
valid.code: declare const record: Record<string, unknown>; Reflect.set(record, 'name', 'Ada');

valid.name: Reflect.set with a variable key on an array - elements store, never transitions the hidden class
valid.code: declare const values: number[]; declare const index: number; Reflect.set(values, index, 1);

valid.name: Reflect.set with a variable key on a typed array - FLOAT64ELEMENTS store, map unchanged
valid.code: declare const buffer: Float64Array; declare const index: number; Reflect.set(buffer, index, 1);

valid.name: Reflect.get with a variable key on a plain object - a read cannot enter dictionary mode
valid.code: declare const record: Record<string, unknown>; declare const key: string; const value = Reflect.get(record, key);

valid.name: write inside the construction primitive's own declaration is exempt - resolved by class, member, and source file, not by name alone
valid.code: export class JsonObject { public static fromEntries<T>(entries: Iterable<readonly [string, T]>): Record<string, T> { const result: Record<string, T> = {}; for (const [key, value] of entries) { result[key] = value; } return result; } }

valid.name: Reflect.set inside the mutation primitive's own declaration is exempt - resolved by class, member, and source file, not by name alone
valid.code: export class JsonObject { public static write(target: object, key: PropertyKey, value: unknown): boolean { if (key === '__proto__') { return false; } const result = Reflect.set(target, key, value); return result; } }
